rows.title: Attach a licensed market-price feed
rows.what: Ingest opening and closing spreads, totals and moneylines for the games we originate; write them into the existing snapshot schema.
rows.why: It is the only change that turns four blank columns into real ones, and it is a prerequisite for every staking number.
rows.risk: Licensing cost; redistribution terms may forbid publishing the numbers even if we hold them.
rows.decide: Budget, vendor, and whether published prices may be shown.

rows.title: Record a manual board snapshot with timestamps while a feed is arranged
rows.what: A human reads a public board at a fixed time and records it with the source and the minute.
rows.why: Produces a real opening/closing pair immediately, which is enough to exercise CLV, ROI and the demotion gates end to end.
rows.risk: Manual entry contradicts the no-manual-input rule and cannot be automated; it would have to be clearly badged.
rows.decide: Whether a badged manual snapshot is acceptable as an interim input.

rows.title: Widen the game log to prior seasons
rows.what: Capture the same official week pages for earlier seasons so ratings start with a prior.
rows.why: Fixes the cold-start problem (a week-1 model knows nothing) and is the only route to a 200-bet sample.
rows.risk: More data invites more multiple testing; the FDR control becomes mandatory rather than optional.
rows.decide: How many seasons to capture and whether to keep them in-repo.

rows.title: Make the injury join a priced input, with a measured effect size
rows.what: Regress margin and total on the replacement-depth features produced here; keep the coefficient only if it survives walk-forward.
rows.why: The join already exists and is the desk's most distinctive asset; unused, it is just a table.
rows.risk: Depth charts are noisy, mostly undated and club-published; a spurious coefficient is easy to fit.
rows.decide: Whether to accept club charts as the depth source (Q-03).

rows.title: Decide the reward rule, scoring signal and staking as two prizes
rows.what: Two awards: best signal (hit rate with n and CI) and best staking (ROI with CI). Neither can buy the other.
rows.why: A single award on staking rewards luck; a single award on signal ignores whether it can be monetised.
rows.risk: Two prizes may fragment attention; a minimum n is needed to qualify for either.
rows.decide: Prize structure, eligibility threshold, who funds it.

rows.title: Automate the capture on a schedule rather than on demand
rows.what: A scheduled workflow captures the official pages weekly, rebuilds, verifies and commits.
rows.why: A snapshot is only an opening or closing number if captures happen at the right times automatically.
rows.risk: Scheduled jobs generate commits and noise; needs a stable parser and a clear failure path.
rows.decide: Whether a scheduled bot may commit to this branch.

rows.title: League-wide per-week player stats feed for props
rows.what: Capture every skill player's per-week receiving/rushing lines instead of five hand-picked players.
rows.why: Five players is an illustration, not a board; prop pricing needs coverage.
rows.risk: Cost and rate limits; hundreds of page fetches per week.
rows.decide: Budget for a stats vendor versus scraping official pages.

rows.title: Publish a settlement rule for every prop market
rows.what: Write down, per market, exactly what settles it and how a stat correction is handled.
rows.why: Without it two people can grade the same bet differently, and no backtest is reproducible.
rows.decide: Adopt the book's rules or the official box score.

rows.title: Add a calibration curve to the moneyline
rows.what: Bin predicted probabilities and plot realised frequency, with n per bin.
rows.why: Brier alone hides whether the model is overconfident in the tails, which is where money is lost.
rows.risk: Small n per bin will make the curve noisy; needs pooling across seasons.

rows.title: Consolidate the older site trees into an archive index
rows.what: One page listing every earlier tree with what it contains and whether it is superseded.
rows.why: A reviewer should not have to guess which of a dozen dashboards is current.
rows.risk: Touches other sessions' files; only the archive index should change.
rows.decide: Which tree is canonical for each topic.
